events.title: Columbus Sights Trinidad
events.description: On his third voyage to the Americas, Christopher Columbus spotted a Caribbean island at midday and named it Trinidad, after the Holy Trinity. His fleet was running low on water and was looking for a safe place to land.
events.significance: This was the first recorded European sighting of Trinidad. It opened a new chapter of Spanish exploration along the northern coast of South America.

events.title: Aurangzeb Proclaimed Mughal Emperor
events.description: After a bitter war of succession against his brothers, Aurangzeb was proclaimed emperor of the Mughal Empire in India.
events.significance: His long reign pushed the Mughal Empire to its greatest territorial extent. It was also marked by costly wars and religious tensions that contributed to the empire's later decline.

events.title: The First U.S. Patent Is Issued
events.description: Samuel Hopkins of Vermont received the first patent granted under the new United States patent system. It covered an improved method of making potash, an ingredient used in fertilizer, soap and glass.
events.significance: The patent began the American system of legally protecting inventions. That system has helped drive innovation in the United States ever since.

events.title: The Battle of Passchendaele Begins
events.description: British and Allied forces launched a major offensive near Ypres in West Flanders, Belgium. Heavy rain and shell-torn ground turned the battlefield into a sea of mud.
events.significance: Passchendaele became one of the best-known symbols of the grinding, costly nature of trench warfare in World War I.

events.title: Apollo 15 Drives on the Moon
events.description: Astronauts David Scott and James Irwin took the Lunar Roving Vehicle on its first drive across the lunar surface.
events.significance: The rover let astronauts travel much farther from their lander than they could on foot. That greatly expanded how much of the Moon they could explore and sample.
